1926, September
FR. SOLANUS, NOTEBOOK NO. 1.
Page 34 Cont.
Sept. 19 Unknown Sickness - complication. Francis Lipka 6 of Kings Mill, Mich, peculiarly helpless & like paralized since 6 weeks old. He never recognizes anyone - parents or others. Parents drive in 65 miles and enroll him perpetualy To-day.
28 James E. Quinlan, 40, St. Ignis Mich. Examined by Mayo Bros Rochester Minn. in June and found to have cancer of stomach and liver; brought to St Ann's Beaupre afterward latter part of July; To-day reported "No improvement." Enrolled 2nd time now
Oct. 2 Blindness Frank J. Boyle 42, foreman in Dodge Br's Factory 1481 Townsend Ave. Enrolled July 13 in S.M.A. for blindness three days before being sent to Specialist in Niles Mich. One Specialist declared "Absolutely hopeless" never to see again. Before leaving for 2nd Specialis he sees his Mother as in tears they kiss Good Bye. Now able to read the newspaper. Thanks be to God! P.S. While testing his eyes at Niles and before treated at all they phone his Mother: "Don't worry Mother, Frank can see."
Oct. 2nd Margarete Borland 2, of 4361 Eastlawn had never walked, was enroll- ed July 15th - same evening started to walk, now running all around.
Oct. 2nd Mrs. Bridget Kelly 54 enrolled two months ago, then a hopeless case of rheumatic paralis for 11 weeks. Her daughter on way home from Detroit gets wire in N.Y. City that "Mother has left hospital and is well."
Oct. 4 Mrs. Mary Sienkiewicz comes to monastery anxious and discouraged - had been roped in by "witch-like" fortunteller"' twelve years ago for ten dollars. Since that time real peace and conjugal confi- dence had been unknown. She brings her husband same p.m. Fr. S. urges
